title: What tells the pop-ups to stay up
ask: Which signal should switch the pop-up relays K1 / K2 to "up", now that their coils must come off O1?
why: D-460 drives the pop-ups the Mazda way: O1 powers each motor's WR, and K1 / K2 steer 12 V to R (up) or RY (down); the motor moves only when its command disagrees with where it is, and stops itself. That only works if the K1 / K2 coils follow "lamps should be up", not O1: a coil on O1 (today's N09) is energised whenever O1 is, so the lamps could only ever go up, and every window press would raise them. No PMU output is free (rules spare-capacity), so the coils need a signal that already exists. The wink switches keep their job either way: a held wink still opens the other side's coil return, so only the winked lamp rises. The relays, the leg and O1 are unchanged by the choice; only the coil feed (N09) and the wink logic move.
options:
(a) The two headlamp outputs O2 (low) and O3 (high) through a pair of diodes into both coils, at the dash node: about $1. The lamps are up whenever a beam is lit and down when both are off. A wink with the lights off lights the low beam for the moment the lamp is up (the PMU raises O2 with O1); the lamp that stays down is lit inside its bucket, which is harmless. Forecloses nothing.
(b) A spare ICU pin through a small transistor on the ICU carrier grounding the coils' return: about $2 and one conductor from the ICU to the node. The lamps can rise unlit for a wink, but the pop-ups then depend on the ICU being up and on firmware (D-409's path for a surprise).
(c) The tail / park output O6: no parts. The lamps rise with the parking lights as well as the headlamps, and a wink only works with the parking lights on.
recommend: (a), unless you want a wink to raise an unlit lamp; then (b)
stops: R-APPLY-01.16 (N09 and K1 / K2 terminal 86 / 85 are re-sourced from the answer); the firmware's pop-up and wink logic; pinning the L2 leg (E21).

title: Room in the front leg for the pop-up wires
ask: How should the front leg carry the pop-ups' extra wires, since its plugs have one free cavity and the Mazda scheme needs more?
why: D-460 counted one more conductor per side. Done the Mazda way each motor takes four: WR (its power, now L2-P 3 / 4), R (up) and RY (down) from K1 / K2, and YG, which is +12 V while the motor runs (00-CAR SP-584), not the contact to ground that A4 / A5 read today. That is up to eight conductors where the leg has four, and the only free cavity is L2-S 6; L2-S 4 and 5 are held for the self-parking wiper (D-317) and the outside-air sensor (D-329). How the PMU knows a lamp is moving also changes, because a +12 V signal cannot sit on the A4 / A5 ground ladders as drawn. CK08 proves the motor's terminals first (R11).
options:
(a) One WR wire to a splice at the nose for both motors (as the headlights are done) in L2-P 3, R / RY in L2-P 4 and L2-S 1, 2 and 6, YG capped at each motor, and the PMU reads "moving" from O1's current instead (it is above the window bus's idle only while a motor runs). No parts. A4 / A5 become the gear-switch ladders alone; the PMU no longer knows which side is moving, only that one is.
(b) A larger signal plug for the front leg (an 8-way in place of L2-S's 6-way, about $6) carrying R / RY for both sides, with YG read on A4 / A5 through a small transistor stage per side at the node (about $2). Keeps the per-side transit sense and the wiper and air-sensor spares.
(c) Use the held L2-S 4 and 5 for R / RY and drop the self-parking-wiper return and the outside-air sensor reservations. No parts; forecloses both.
recommend: (a), unless you want the PMU to know which lamp is stuck; then (b)
stops: R-APPLY-01.16 (the L2 cavities for N12-N15, the A4 / A5 ladders, the pop-up cycle rule); pinning the L2 leg (E21); the drawings for the L2 leg.

title: What the fuel pump does when the oil sender wire is shorted
ask: Should a sender wire shorted to the body also stop the fuel pump after the prime, as an open one now does?
why: D-461 made an OPEN sender read as zero oil pressure, so the pump stops after the 3 s prime. A sender wire SHORTED to the body reads the opposite way: like enormous oil pressure, because the sender's resistance falls as pressure rises (00-CAR SP-787). D-249 counted any fault as "oil OK, keep pumping", and D-461 did not say whether that still holds for a short. A crash can short the wire as easily as break it; then, with the key left on, the pump keeps running. A real sender never reads a dead short, so the PMU can tell a short apart from high pressure.
options:
(a) A short also stops the pump after the prime: the cluster shows a sender fault, and the engine stops. Safest in a crash; a chafed sender wire then strands you just as a broken one does. No parts.
(b) A short keeps the pump running, as D-249 had it: a chafed wire never strands you, but in a crash that shorts it the pump runs while the key is on. No parts.
recommend: (a), unless you would rather never be stranded by a chafed sender wire
stops: the FUEL_PUMP rule's short case (logic FUEL_PUMP, inputs A7); the firmware's oil gate.

title: Which door switch lights the dome lamp
ask: Which switch should ground the dome lamp's DOOR contact when a door opens, now that the lamp is off the PMU?
why: D-462 puts the dome lamp back on the factory circuit: an always-hot fuse (F12, now on the busbar) and "its own door switch". In the factory car the lamp's DOOR contact (RY) is grounded by the door switches PT644 (00-CAR PT957, SP-720). This build replaced those with new plunger switches (DV41, from the P084 6-pack) that each ground through a resistor into the PMU's door ladder A6, so they cannot also ground the lamp directly: the lamp's 12 V would back-feed A6 and read as a fault. Until this is answered the DOOR position does nothing; ON and OFF work.
options:
(a) A second plunger in each B-pillar jamb, beside the A6 one, on RY to the lamp: the P084 pack has one spare, so one more 6-pack (about $15) or a pair; two holes drilled, one in each jamb, and one more conductor up the C-pillar with the lamp's run (RT23).
(b) Keep the one plunger per door and add a diode in each A6 resistor branch so the same switch also grounds RY: a few cents, no holes, but the A6 ladder's values are re-worked (each door reads about 0.6 V higher) and proved again.
(c) No door position: the dome lamp works on its ON switch only. No parts, no wire; the door no longer lights it.
recommend: (b), unless you would rather not touch the A6 ladder; then (a)
stops: the dome lamp's DOOR wiring (DV39, L4-M 8, RT23, the L4 leg's door branch); with (b), the A6 ladder values (ladders, the sim).
